lessons.title: Tracking Income and Expenses
lessons.body: As a reseller, every naira, shilling, or cedi that comes in and goes out must be recorded. Without tracking, you are guessing. Start with a simple notebook or a free spreadsheet like Google Sheets. Create columns for date, description, income (money received), and expenses (money spent). For example, on 1st March you buy 20 phone cases at 500 each from a supplier in Lagos, spending 10,000. That is an expense. On 5th March you sell 15 cases at 1,200 each, earning 18,000. That is income. Record every single transaction, even small ones like transport to the market or airtime for calls to customers. If you use a smartphone, apps like Wave or Kippa are designed for small businesses in Africa and can send reminders. At the end of each week, total your income and expenses. This habit shows you exactly where your money goes. Many resellers fail because they mix personal and business cash. Open a separate bank account or mobile money wallet for your business. Use a dedicated SIM card for business calls. When you track properly, you can answer simple questions: Did I make a profit last month? Which product sells best? Where can I cut costs? Without tracking, you might feel busy but be losing money. Set a fixed time each day, say 8 PM, to update your records. It takes 10 minutes. Do it consistently. After one month, you will have real data to guide your decisions. Remember, tracking is not for tax alone; it is for your own survival and growth. Start today with a notebook and pen if you have nothing else. The goal is to know your numbers.

lessons.title: Calculating Profit and Loss
lessons.body: Profit is what remains after you subtract all costs from your sales. Loss is when costs exceed sales. To calculate profit, you need two numbers: total revenue (all money from sales) and total expenses (all money spent to buy and sell goods). For example, you sell 50 bags at 2,000 each, revenue = 100,000. Your expenses: buying bags at 1,200 each = 60,000, transport = 5,000, packaging = 2,000, airtime and data = 3,000. Total expenses = 70,000. Profit = 100,000 - 70,000 = 30,000. That is your gross profit. But you also have overheads like rent for storage, electricity, or wages for a helper. Subtract those to get net profit. If net profit is negative, you have a loss. Many resellers forget to include their own time or transport. For instance, if you spend 2,000 on bus fare to meet a supplier, that is an expense. Track every cost. Use a simple formula: Profit = Sales - (Cost of Goods Sold + Operating Expenses). Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) is what you paid for the items you sold. If you bought 100 bags but only sold 50, COGS is for 50 bags only, not 100. The remaining 50 are inventory, not an expense yet. This is a common mistake. Also, calculate profit per item: selling price minus buying price. If you buy at 1,200 and sell at 2,000, profit per bag is 800. Then multiply by number sold. This helps you decide which products to focus on. If a product gives low profit, drop it. Review your profit and loss weekly or monthly. Write it down. Compare months to see if you are improving. If you are making a loss, find out why: Are prices too low? Are expenses too high? Adjust quickly. Profit is not optional; it is the reason you are in business.

lessons.title: Managing Cash Flow
lessons.body: Cash flow is the movement of money in and out of your business. You can be profitable on paper but still run out of cash to pay suppliers or transport. This happens when customers owe you money or when you spend too much on stock that sits unsold. For example, you have 50,000 in sales but 40,000 is on credit from customers who will pay next month. Meanwhile, you need 30,000 to buy new stock today. You have no cash. To manage cash flow, follow these rules: First, collect payments immediately. If you sell on credit, set clear terms: payment within 7 days. Follow up politely but firmly. Second, don't overstock. Buy only what you can sell in 2-3 weeks. Use the 50/30/20 rule: 50% of cash for restocking, 30% for expenses, 20% as reserve. Third, negotiate credit from your suppliers. Ask for 14 days to pay after delivery. This gives you time to sell and collect cash before paying. Fourth, keep a cash flow forecast. On a sheet, list expected cash in (from sales) and cash out (for purchases, transport, rent) for the next 4 weeks. If you see a shortfall, arrange a small loan from a microfinance bank or a family member early. Fifth, separate personal and business cash. Never use business cash for personal needs like school fees. Pay yourself a small salary. Tools like Kippa or Wave can help track cash. Also, mobile money statements show your balance. Review daily. If you have surplus cash, save it for slow months. Cash flow problems kill more reselling businesses than lack of profit. Stay on top of it.

lessons.title: Tax Deductions for Resellers
lessons.body: Tax deductions reduce the amount of income tax you pay. As a reseller, you can deduct ordinary and necessary expenses used to run your business. In many African countries, small businesses with turnover below a threshold (e.g., 25 million Naira in Nigeria) may pay a simplified tax or be exempt, but you still need records. Common deductions include: cost of goods sold (what you paid for items you resold), transport to buy or deliver goods, packaging materials, airtime and data for business calls, rent for storage or shop, salaries for helpers, and fees for accounting software. For example, if your revenue is 500,000 and you spent 300,000 on goods, 20,000 on transport, 10,000 on packaging, your taxable profit is 170,000. Without deductions, you would pay tax on 500,000. Keep receipts for every expense. A receipt can be a handwritten note from a supplier, a mobile money transfer screenshot, or a store invoice. If you buy from an open market without receipts, write the details in your record book and ask the seller to sign. In some countries, you can deduct a portion of your home rent if you use part of your home as an office. Also, depreciation on equipment like a laptop or scale can be deducted over time. To claim deductions, you must file your tax returns. Many revenue authorities now allow online filing. If you are unsure, visit a local tax office or ask a business association. Do not ignore tax; penalties can be high. But do not overpay by missing deductions. A simple spreadsheet can track deductible expenses. At the end of the year, total them and subtract from your income. This lowers your tax bill legally. Always keep records for at least 5 years.

lessons.title: Using Accounting Software
lessons.body: Accounting software makes tracking, profit calculation, and tax preparation easier. You don't need to be an accountant to use it. Start with free or low-cost tools designed for African small businesses. Wave (waveapps.com) is free for basic accounting and works on a smartphone. Kippa is a Nigerian app that helps you record sales, expenses, and debts, and sends reminders. For more features, try QuickBooks Online or Zoho Books; they have monthly plans around $10-20. If you sell on Jumia or Konga, their seller dashboards show sales and fees. To get started, download the app, create a business profile, and set up your chart of accounts: categories like Sales, Cost of Goods Sold, Transport, Rent, etc. Then, every time you make a sale or spend money, enter it. The software automatically calculates profit and loss. You can also attach photos of receipts. For cash flow, many apps show a dashboard with money in and out. Some integrate with mobile money or bank feeds, so transactions import automatically. If you have no smartphone, use a simple Excel template. Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets has free templates for income and expense tracking. The key is consistency: enter data daily. At month-end, generate reports: profit and loss, cash flow, and expense breakdown. These reports help you make decisions: Which product is most profitable? Where can you cut costs? They also make tax filing simple because you have all numbers ready. If you have multiple staff, you can give them limited access. Training: watch YouTube tutorials for your chosen app. Many are free. Start with one tool and master it. Do not jump between apps. A good software saves time and reduces errors. It also gives you confidence when applying for a loan, as you can show clean records.

lessons.title: Budgeting for Growth
lessons.body: A budget is a plan for how you will spend and save money to grow your reselling business. Without a budget, you may spend on impulse and never expand. Start by reviewing your last 3 months of income and expenses. Identify your average monthly profit. For example, if you make 50,000 profit per month, decide how much to reinvest. A common rule: reinvest 50%, save 30%, and use 20% for personal needs. Your growth budget should include: increasing stock of best-selling items, marketing (e.g., printing flyers, boosting posts on Facebook or Instagram), buying equipment (e.g., a weighing scale, a smartphone for better product photos), and training (e.g., a course on customer service). Set specific goals: âIn 6 months, I will double my sales by adding two new products and saving 100,000 for bulk purchases.â Then break it down monthly. For instance, save 15,000 per month for bulk buying, spend 10,000 on ads, and 5,000 on packaging. Track your actual spending against the budget each month. If you overspend on transport, adjust next month. Use a simple envelope system: put cash for each category in separate envelopes. For digital money, use mobile money wallets or a spreadsheet. Also, build an emergency fund: aim for 3 months of expenses. This protects you from shocks like price hikes or delayed payments. When you stick to a budget, you can afford to take calculated risks, like buying a larger quantity at a discount. Review your budget quarterly. As your business grows, increase your reinvestment. But always pay yourself a small salary to stay motivated. Budgeting is not about restricting; it is about directing your money to where it works best. With a plan, you move from survival to growth.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of tracking income and expenses?
options: A) To impress customers
B) To know your financial position
C) To increase prices
D) To avoid paying tax
quiz.explanation: Tracking helps you understand where money comes from and goes, enabling informed decisions.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of an expense for a reseller?
options: A) Money received from a customer
B) A loan from a bank
C) Transport fare to buy goods
D) Personal savings
quiz.explanation: Transport fare to buy goods is a cost incurred in running the business.

quiz.q: Why should you separate personal and business cash?
options: A) To confuse tax authorities
B) To easily track business performance
C) To spend more on personal items
D) To avoid using mobile money
quiz.explanation: Separating cash prevents mixing and allows accurate calculation of business profit.

quiz.q: Which tool is recommended for a reseller with no formal training to track finances?
options: A) A complex accounting textbook
B) A simple notebook or Google Sheets
C) A professional accountant
D) A bank statement only
quiz.explanation: A notebook or spreadsheet is accessible and easy to use for beginners.

quiz.q: How often should you update your financial records?
options: A) Once a year
B) Only when you remember
C) Daily or at least weekly
D) When tax is due
quiz.explanation: Regular updates ensure accuracy and prevent backlog.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: A) Total money received from sales
B) Total expenses minus total revenue
C) Total revenue minus total expenses
D) The amount of cash in your pocket
quiz.explanation: Profit is what remains after subtracting all costs from sales revenue.

quiz.q: If you buy 100 items at 500 each and sell 60 at 800 each, what is your gross profit?
quiz.explanation: Revenue from 60 items = 60*800=48,000; COGS for 60 items = 60*500=30,000; profit = 18,000.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT included in Cost of Goods Sold?
options: A) Purchase price of items sold
B) Transport to bring goods to your shop
C) Rent for your personal apartment
D) Packaging for the items sold
quiz.explanation: Personal rent is not a business expense and not part of COGS.

quiz.q: What is net profit?
options: A) Gross profit minus operating expenses
B) Total sales minus cost of goods sold
C) Total revenue plus expenses
D) The same as gross profit
quiz.explanation: Net profit accounts for all expenses, including overheads, after gross profit.

quiz.q: Why is it important to calculate profit per item?
options: A) To decide which products to focus on
B) To increase the selling price
C) To reduce the buying price
D) To impress suppliers
quiz.explanation: Profit per item shows which products are most profitable, guiding inventory decisions.

quiz.q: What is cash flow?
options: A) The movement of money in and out of your business
B) The total profit you make
C) The amount of stock you have
D) The money you owe suppliers
quiz.explanation: Cash flow tracks the timing of cash receipts and payments.

quiz.q: Why can a profitable business run out of cash?
options: A) Because profit is not real
B) Because customers pay on credit and suppliers demand cash
C) Because taxes are too high
D) Because accounting software is expensive
quiz.explanation: Timing mismatches between cash inflows and outflows cause cash shortages.

quiz.q: What is a good strategy to improve cash flow?
options: A) Sell more on credit
B) Buy more stock than you can sell
C) Collect payments immediately
D) Use business cash for personal needs
quiz.explanation: Immediate payment collection ensures cash is available for business needs.

quiz.q: What does the 50/30/20 rule for cash flow suggest?
options: A) 50% for restocking, 30% for expenses, 20% as reserve
B) 50% for savings, 30% for personal, 20% for business
C) 50% for marketing, 30% for stock, 20% for tax
D) 50% for loans, 30% for rent, 20% for transport
quiz.explanation: This rule allocates cash to restocking, expenses, and reserves for stability.

quiz.q: How can you manage cash flow if you expect a shortfall?
options: A) Ignore it and hope for the best
B) Arrange a small loan early
C) Spend more on marketing
D) Delay paying suppliers
quiz.explanation: Early action, like a loan, prevents disruption when cash is tight.

quiz.q: What is a tax deduction?
options: A) An expense that reduces taxable income
B) A penalty for late tax filing
C) A tax refund from government
D) A type of business loan
quiz.explanation: Deductions lower the income on which tax is calculated.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a deductible expense for a reseller?
options: A) Personal school fees
B) Transport to deliver goods to customers
C) Buying a television for home
D) Donations to a political party
quiz.explanation: Transport for business delivery is an ordinary and necessary business expense.

quiz.q: Why should you keep receipts for business expenses?
options: A) To prove deductions to tax authorities
B) To decorate your office
C) To increase your sales
D) To avoid paying suppliers
quiz.explanation: Receipts are evidence required to claim tax deductions.

quiz.q: In many African countries, small businesses with turnover below a threshold may:
options: A) Pay no tax at all
B) Pay a simplified tax or be exempt
C) Pay double tax
D) Only pay tax on personal income
quiz.explanation: Simplified tax regimes exist to support small businesses.

quiz.q: What is depreciation?
options: A) The increase in value of an asset
B) The decrease in value of an asset over time
C) A type of tax
D) A business expense that is not deductible
quiz.explanation: Depreciation spreads the cost of an asset over its useful life.

quiz.q: Which accounting software is free for basic use?
options: A) QuickBooks Online
B) Wave
C) Zoho Books
D) Sage
quiz.explanation: Wave offers free basic accounting features.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of using accounting software?
options: A) It automatically calculates profit and loss
B) It eliminates the need for receipts
C) It guarantees more sales
D) It replaces the need for a bank account
quiz.explanation: Software automates calculations, saving time and reducing errors.

quiz.q: Which app is designed for Nigerian small businesses to record sales and debts?
options: A) Kippa
B) Excel
C) WhatsApp
D) Facebook
quiz.explanation: Kippa is a Nigerian app for small business record-keeping.

quiz.q: What should you do before choosing accounting software?
options: A) Buy the most expensive one
B) Identify your business needs and budget
C) Ask a friend to choose for you
D) Wait until tax season
quiz.explanation: Choosing based on needs and budget ensures you get value.

quiz.q: How can accounting software help with tax filing?
options: A) It pays tax for you
B) It generates reports with all income and expenses
C) It hides income from tax authorities
D) It reduces your tax rate
quiz.explanation: Reports make it easy to fill tax returns accurately.

quiz.q: What is a budget?
options: A) A plan for spending and saving money
B) A record of past expenses
C) A loan from a bank
D) A list of customers
quiz.explanation: A budget is a forward-looking financial plan.

quiz.q: Why is budgeting important for growth?
options: A) It restricts all spending
B) It helps you allocate money to growth activities
C) It guarantees profit
D) It eliminates the need for tracking
quiz.explanation: Budgeting directs funds to areas that expand the business.

quiz.q: What is a recommended reinvestment percentage from profit for growth?
quiz.explanation: Reinvesting 50% of profit is a common guideline for growth.

quiz.q: What is an emergency fund?
options: A) Money set aside for personal luxury
B) Money saved to cover unexpected business expenses
C) A loan from a microfinance bank
D) A type of tax deduction
quiz.explanation: An emergency fund provides a cushion for unforeseen events.

quiz.q: How often should you review your budget?
options: A) Every day
B) Every week
C) Quarterly
D) Every five years
quiz.explanation: Quarterly reviews allow adjustments as business conditions change.

quiz.q: What is the envelope system?
options: A) Putting cash for each budget category in separate envelopes
B) Sending invoices in envelopes
C) Saving money in a bank envelope
D) A method of tax filing
quiz.explanation: The envelope system helps control spending by category.
